intent: Repair bucket_catch/packages/frontend's typecheck so `npm run build` works again and eslint actually runs, before splitting the two over-cap files in that package.
scope: Non-goal: the 45 eslint errors this change makes visible; they are pre-existing and tracked separately
Non-goal: any change to the coverage thresholds or exclude list in vite.config.ts
changes: vitest 4 no longer contributes the `test` key to vite's own defineConfig, so the `/// <reference types="vitest" />` triple-slash directive had gone inert and `test: {...}` was an unknown property (TS2769). Switched the import to vitest/config, which is the canonical vitest-4 typing, and replaced the dead directive with a comment saying why.

Dropped the unused `const { result } =` destructuring at usePuzzleGameLoop.test.ts:231 (TS6133), keeping the renderHook call itself. The test asserts on mockCtx.drawImage rather than on the hook's return, so the binding was dead; the following test in the same file already calls renderHook bare.

verification.evidence: Exit 0, 52 modules transformed, bundle 314.17 kB. This command FAILED at HEAD on both TS2769 and TS6133, so the package could not build before this change.

14 test files, 145 tests passed; Statements 100% (583/583), Branches 100% (217/217), Functions 100% (97/97), Lines 100% (534/534) — identical to the pre-change baseline. This is what proves vite.config.ts is still being read after changing its import: had the config stopped applying, jsdom would be gone and the suite would fail rather than pass at identical totals, and the 100% thresholds would no longer be enforced.

Exits 1, reporting 45 errors across 10 files. This is NOT a regression and NOT a restored-green claim: `lint` is `tsc --noEmit && eslint src`, and because tsc was failing at HEAD the `&&` short-circuited, so eslint had never run on this package at all. Fixing tsc unmasked 45 pre-existing eslint errors — 18 no-non-null-assertion, 10 unbound-method, 9 non-nullable-type-assertion-style, 5 no-unnecessary-type-assertion, plus require-await, no-this-alias and no-deprecated. Fixing them needs per-site judgment and is out of scope for this commit.

verification.command: npx eslint on the two over-cap files, as a pre-split baseline
verification.evidence: src/hooks/usePuzzleGameLoop.ts: 2 errors. src/hooks/usePuzzleGameLoop.test.ts: 7 errors. Captured so the upcoming split can be checked differentially — after it, the package total must still be 45 and the new files may carry only errors that travelled with the moved code.
All configured hooks pass on the two touched files.

risks: This package has no CI workflow and is not covered by pre-commit, which is how a non-building, non-linting state persisted unnoticed. Nothing added here prevents a recurrence; wiring CI for bucket_catch is a separate piece of work.

45 eslint errors are now visible and will stay red until addressed. Anyone running `npm run lint` here will see failures where they previously saw a (misleading) short-circuit failure on tsc alone. The visible state is worse-looking but strictly more honest.

Dropping the unused binding leaves that test asserting only on the canvas mock. It was already doing so — the binding was never read — so this documents an existing narrowness rather than creating one. Adding assertions would be a behaviour change and is out of scope.
rollback: git revert the commit — two edited files, no data, config or schema migration.
After rollback, expect npm run build and npm run lint to fail again on TS2769 and TS6133, and npm run coverage to still pass at 583/217/97/534.
